mainTopic: Sides count as 'in front' (from הזאה); silence when the ספר תורה is opened; washing hands and the ברכה and prayers of the כהנים at נשיאת כפים
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about sprinkling (הזאה). It shows that sprinkling toward the sides in front of a person still counts as sprinkling 'forward,' so the sides are treated as 'in front.' רבא בר רב הונא then rules that once a ספר תורה is opened, one may not talk, even about הלכה. רבי זירא, in the name of רב חסדא, brings a different פסוק for the same rule. רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כהן must wash his hands before נשיאת כפים. רבי אלעזר בן שמוע tells his students that three habits of respect earned him a long life, one of which was always saying a ברכה before blessing the people. The גמרא then gives the words the כהן says at three moments: the ברכה before blessing, a prayer as he starts walking up, and a prayer when he turns away at the end. That last prayer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sprinkling to the front sides still counts as forward
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about הזאה ends: switching between forward and backward ruins the sprinkling, but aiming forward and hitting the front sides is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he meant to sprinkle forward and sprinkled backward, or meant backward and sprinkled forward, the sprinkling is invalid. If he meant forward and sprinkled toward the sides in front of him, the sprinkling is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about sprinkling purifying water. It uses the ruling to show that the sides in front of a person count as 'in front.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's intention for the direction of a הזאה matters, so mixing up front and back makes it invalid. But hitting the sides in front of him does not count as a change from 'forward,' so it stays valid. This supports the idea that people standing at the sides are treated as 'in front.'
steps.whatToRemember: The sides in front of a person count as 'in front.' Sprinkling there matches an intention to sprinkle forward.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The opening words of the ברייתא, 'if he meant to sprinkle forward,' came just before this section.

phrases.english: and he sprinkled backward,
or meant backward and sprinkled forward — his sprinkling is invalid.
If he meant forward and sprinkled toward the sides that are in front of him,
— his sprinkling is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפָנָיו וְהִזָּה עַל צְדָדִין שֶׁבְּפָנָיו הַזָּאָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that the גמרא brought just before this section as support.
steps.raayaObject: That the sides in front of a person are treated as 'in front'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the direction of הזאה

steps.title: No talking once the Torah scroll is opened
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא rules that once a ספר תורה is opened, talking is forbidden, even about הלכה. He learns it from עזרא opening the scroll, when the people 'stood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said: once a ספר תורה is opened, it is forbidden to talk, even about a matter of הלכה. The פסוק says 'when he opened it, all the people stood,' and 'standing' means silence, as another פסוק says: 'they do not speak, because they stood, they answered no more.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבא בר רב הונא forbids any talking once the ספר תורה is open, and he proves it with two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the people 'stood' when עזרא opened the scroll. The second פסוק, from איוב, shows that 'standing' can mean being silent. Put together, opening the scroll calls for silence, and this applies even to Torah talk.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of staying completely silent during קריאת התורה.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna says:
Once a Torah scroll has been opened,
it is forbidden to talk, even about a matter of halacha,
as it says: "And when he opened it, all the people stood,"
phrases.notes: נחמיה 8:5. Here עזרא is opening the Torah in front of the people.

phrases.english: and "standing" means nothing other than silence,
as it says: "And shall I wait, because they do not speak,
because they stood still, they answered no more?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּפְתַּח סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to synagogue practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a ספר תורה is opened, all talking is forbidden, even about הלכה.

steps.title: A different verse for the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, in the name of רב חסדא, learns the same rule from 'the ears of all the people were toward the Torah scroll.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: we learn it from here: 'And the ears of all the people were toward the Torah scroll.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second source is given for the same law of silence. It uses a more direct פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the two-step proof from 'standing,' this פסוק says plainly that everyone's ears were turned to the ספר תורה. If you are listening only to the Torah, you cannot be talking or listening to anything else. The rule stays the same; only the source changes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said: from here:
"And the ears of all the people were toward the Torah scroll."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the rule in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of silence during the Torah reading comes from the people's ears being turned toward the ספר תורה.

steps.title: A כהן must wash his hands before blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a כהן who has not washed his hands may not do נשיאת כפים, based on 'lift your hands in holiness and bless.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: any כהן who did not wash his hands may not lift his hands to bless, as it says: 'Lift up your hands in holiness and bless ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about ברכת כהנים: the כהן must wash his hands first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links lifting the hands with 'holiness.' Washing is what makes the hands holy before the blessing. Without washing, the כהן may not bless.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that כהנים wash their hands before they go up to bless.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
Any kohen who did not wash his hands
— may not lift his hands to bless,
as it says: "Lift up your hands in holiness
and bless the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁלֹּא נָטַל יָדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of ברכת כהנים with a new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן must wash his hands before נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: Students ask how their teacher lived so long
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע ask him what merit gave him a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: in what merit did you live so long?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story begins. The students' question sets up their teacher's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a great sage what earned him long life is a common way to bring out special good habits. The answer will include a habit about ברכת כהנים, which connects to the topic of the last few teachings.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua:
In what merit did you live a long life?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ בַּמָּה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that will touch on ברכת כהנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What merit earned רבי אלעזר בן שמוע his long life

steps.title: Three habits of respect
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע names three habits: he never used a בית הכנסת as a shortcut, never stepped over people's heads, and never blessed as a כהן without first saying a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: in all my days I never made the בית הכנסת into a shortcut, I never stepped over the heads of the holy people, and I never lifted my hands to bless without a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע answers his students with three habits of respect, one for each part of his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two habits show respect for the בית הכנסת and for the people sitting in it. The third connects to ברכת כהנים: he always said the ברכה before blessing the people.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy people (those gathered to learn or pray)

steps.whatToRemember: Respect for the בית הכנסת, for the people in it, and for the מצוה of ברכת כהנים is presented as a merit for long life.

phrases.english: He said to them: In all my days,
I never made the synagogue into a shortcut,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא פָּסַעְתִּי עַל רָאשֵׁי עַם קוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and I never stepped over the heads of the holy people,
phrases.notes: He means climbing over people seated on the floor to reach his place.

phrases.english: and I never lifted my hands to bless without a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן מִיָּמַי לֹא עָשִׂיתִי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת קַפֶּנְדַּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three habits: never using a בית הכנסת as a shortcut, never stepping over people's heads, and never doing נשיאת כפים without a ברכה.

steps.title: What is the ברכה before blessing the people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact words of the ברכה a כהן says before נשיאת כפים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what words make up the ברכה that רבי אלעזר בן שמוע said before blessing the people. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 told us that a כהן should say a ברכה before blessing the people, but it did not give the wording. Now the גמרא asks for the actual text.

phrases.english: What blessing does he recite?
phrases.notes: The ברכה from step 6, the one the כהן says before he blesses the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the wording of the ברכה mentioned in רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact text of the ברכה said before נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: The wording of the ברכה before נשיאת כפים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, quoting רב חסדא, gives the text: 'אשר קדשנו בקדושתו של אהרן וצונו לברך את עמו ישראל באהבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: 'Who made us holy with the holiness of אהרן and commanded us to bless His people ישראל with love.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא, quoting רב חסדא, gives the exact words of the ברכה the כהנים say before they bless the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה connects the כהנים to the holiness of אהרן, the first כהן. It also says the מצוה is to bless the people 'with love.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ברכה the כהנים still say today before ברכת כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said:
"Who has sanctified us with the sanctity of Aaron
phrases.notes: The usual opening, 'Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the world,' is understood to come before these words.

phrases.aramaic: וְצִוָּנוּ לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַהֲבָה״.
phrases.english: and commanded us to bless His people Israel with love."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה is 'אשר קדשנו בקדושתו של אהרן וצונו לברך את עמו ישראל באהבה'.

steps.title: What does the כהן say when he starts walking up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כהן says when he first moves to go up and bless the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he lifts his feet to go up, what does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question: what prayer the כהן says at the moment he starts walking toward the front. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה in step 8 is said right before the blessing. Now the גמרא goes back to an earlier moment, when the כהן first leaves his place, and asks whether there is a prayer for that point too.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifted his feet, meaning he started walking

phrases.english: When he uproots his feet
phrases.notes: Literally 'pulls up his legs': he starts walking to the place where the כהנים bless the people.

phrases.english: what does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about another prayer connected to נשיאת כפים, this time at an earlier moment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The prayer said when the כהן begins walking up to bless the people.

steps.title: A prayer that the blessing will have no mistake
steps.stepSummary: The כהן prays that the blessing he was commanded to give will not contain any stumbling or sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that this blessing You commanded us to give Your people ישראל will not have in it any stumbling or sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the prayer the כהן says as he starts walking: he asks that his blessing will not contain any mistake or sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request, not a ברכה on the מצוה. The כהן asks ה׳ to help him do the מצוה properly, without any problem that would spoil the blessing.

phrases.english: May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that this blessing which You commanded us
to bless Your people Israel,
shall not contain any stumbling block or sin.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He prays that the blessing will have no stumbling block or sin in it.

steps.title: What does the כהן say when he turns away at the end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כהן says when he finishes and turns his face away from the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he turns his face away from the people, what does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a third question about the end of נשיאת כפים, when the כהן turns away from the people. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have three moments: walking up (step 9), the ברכה right before blessing (step 8), and turning away at the end. The גמרא wants a prayer for this last moment too.

phrases.english: And when he turns his face away from the congregation
what does he say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ מִצִּיבּוּרָא מַאי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of prayers, now moving to the end of נשיאת כפים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The prayer said after the blessing, when the כהן turns away from the people.

steps.title: We did what You asked, now You do your part
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא taught רב עוקבא that the כהן says: 'Master of the world, we have done what You decreed on us; do with us...'. The prayer continues after this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא told רב עוקבא to teach publicly: 'Master of the world, we have done what You decreed on us; now do with us...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tells רב עוקבא what the כהן says at the end, and רב עוקבא teaches it publicly. The prayer is only partly quoted here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים say that they have done their part by blessing the people as ה׳ commanded. Now they ask ה׳ to do His part, and the rest of the request comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He guided him or told him what to say

steps.confusionAlert: The prayer is cut off at 'עשה עמנו'. It is not finished. The rest of what the כהנים ask for comes right after this.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב עוּקְבָא וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda instructed Rav Ukva, and he taught:
phrases.notes: רב חסדא gave רב עוקבא the wording, and רב עוקבא taught it to the public.

phrases.english: "Master of the Universe,
we have done what You decreed upon us;
do with us

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב עוּקְבָא וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן says: 'רבונו של עולם, we have done what You decreed upon us; do with us...', and the prayer continues in the next section.
